item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

turns.text: Could you make an explainer about why we hear echoes? I remember wondering about that as a kid, so it feels like a fun thing to explain. What I have in mind is a 10-second vertical video with a voice-over, and I'd like you to write the words yourself. Please keep the explanation easy for kids to understand. You can choose the look, since I don't have a particular visual style in mind.

Here’s the ready-to-use **10-second vertical explainer**:

**Voice-over:**  
“An echo is your voice bouncing back! Sound hits something far away, like a cliff, then returns to your ears. Hello again!”

**Visuals:**  
A friendly cartoon fox calls across a colorful canyon. Glowing sound waves travel to a cliff, bounce off it, and return to the fox’s ears. The fox smiles as the echo arrives.

args.name: Why We Hear Echoes — Kids Explainer

style.prompt: Create a 10-second vertical educational explainer for young kids, with clear English voice-over and playful colorful 2D cartoon animation. A friendly cartoon fox stands on the left of a spacious canyon facing a distant tall cliff on the right. Visually explain an echo accurately: the fox calls, bright curved sound-wave arcs travel from the fox across the air to the distant rock cliff, reflect off the cliff, and travel back to the fox's ears; the fox smiles as the reflected sound returns. Make the outward journey and reflected return sequential and very easy to follow. Keep the fox and cliff in view in a clean wide composition within the vertical frame, with a gentle camera push in. Warm inviting colors, simple shapes, uncluttered background. One warm friendly adult narrator delivers this exact voice-over clearly at a natural brisk pace, starting immediately and finishing within 10 seconds: 'An echo is your voice bouncing back! Sound hits something far away, like a cliff, then returns to your ears. Hello again!' Narration is the primary audio and must be intelligible, no music, no competing speech. No written text or labels. Ensure the sound waves visibly reflect off the solid cliff rather than appearing spontaneously.
